cards.text: Isaiah the prophet brings a message about two gods, Bel and Nebo. Bel crouches. Nebo cowers, and their idols weigh down beasts and cattle.

cards.question: Bel and Nebo's idols are piled onto beasts and cattle. What does Isaiah say those idols are to the weary animal?

cards.text: Think about that, friend. You pray to a god, and your god needs a RIDE. And the gods just cower and crouch together.

cards.question: Bel and Nebo are able to relieve the burden.
Bel and Nebo are unable to relieve the burden. Where does Isaiah say the gods themselves go?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to the house of Jacob, all who are left of the house of Israel. And He flips the whole picture around.

cards.question: Bel and Nebo have to be carried. What does the LORD say He has done for the house of Jacob since birth?
The LORD tells the house of Jacob that His care for them will stop once they grow old.

cards.text: He'll bear them up even when they turn gray. Friend, MY edges went soft with age, and I got slid into a junk drawer.

cards.question: The LORD promises to carry Israel, sustain them and deliver them. What does He say He has already done for them?

cards.text: Then the LORD asks, "To whom will you compare Me, that we should be alike?" Good luck with that one, friend.
Then He shows what people do. They pour out bags of gold, weigh out silver on scales, and hire a goldsmith.

cards.question: The goldsmith shapes the gold into a ___ so the people can bow down and worship.

cards.text: Then they lift it to their shoulders and carry it along. Another god that needs a RIDE.

cards.question: The people set their gold god down in its place. What does it do once it's there?

answers.text: It doesn't budge from that spot
It falls on its face at night
It slowly turns toward the east

cards.text: Not budging from one spot? I did that for YEARS in a junk drawer, and nobody ever prayed to ME. But these people cry out to theirs.

cards.question: When the people cry out to their gold god, it answers and saves them from their troubles.

cards.text: Now the LORD calls out to transgressors: remember this, take it to heart and be brave. And remember what happened long ago.

cards.question: As He tells them to remember what happened long ago, the LORD says there are other gods like Him.

cards.text: The LORD says He declares the end from the beginning. Friend, I can't even tell you how a batch turns out until the timer goes off.

cards.question: The LORD declares the end from the beginning, and He says His purpose will ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He's summoning someone from the east, from a far-off land.

cards.question: What picture does the LORD use for the one He summons from the east?

cards.text: He calls him a man for His purpose. From a far-off land, friend. I get winded hopping my gold base from one oven to the next.

cards.question: The LORD says His plan for the man from the east might not come to pass.

cards.text: The LORD says, "Listen to Me," and calls them stubborn people, far removed from righteousness.

cards.question: The people are far removed from righteousness. What does the LORD say He is doing with His righteousness?
The LORD says His salvation will not be delayed, and He will grant salvation to ___.

cards.text: And He'll adorn Israel with His splendor. Friend, I spent years covered in dust. SPLENDOR is a serious upgrade.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the idols 'weigh down beasts and cattle,' and the question adds 'piled onto' and 'the weary animal.' Together these give away the answer 'A burdensome load' and rule out 'A shade from the sun' and 'A guide on the road' before the baker reasons anything.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 6 says the LORD 'flips the whole picture around,' and the question opens with 'Bel and Nebo have to be carried.' Together they point straight to 'Carried them along' and rule out both wrong answers. 'Left them to walk alone' and 'Watched them from far away' are the opposite of a flip, so no baker would pick them.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Stop 1 has 5 multiple choice cards, 3 true or false and only 1 fill in the blank (card 13). Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'Good luck with that one, friend.' is a mild, pleasant tag, not a real laugh. The moment (God asking who could compare to Him) can hold a stronger reaction.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Several story cards are plain retelling with none of Papa Dorin's voice: stop 1 cards 1 and 12, and stop 2 cards 1, 5 and 9. Stop 2 card 5 is a single bare sentence. Together they make long parts of the walkthrough read like a summary, not like Papa Dorin telling it.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
